chapter_theme: A single short song at Kulandai (குளந்தைநகர்): fear of dying in the pit of women's delusion, and trust that no one but Murugan can give the boon.

953.reading: The poet asks that, falling under the sway of women with wave-like hair, bow-brows, poison eyes and drum-like waists into the wide pit of delusion, he not give up his life to Death in fear and suffering; if Murugan does not grant the boon, who else will? The praise names him the one who circled the earth on the peacock, the groom of the Kura girl, and the lord of the temple at Kulandai.
953.nuance: வரம் தராவிடில் பிறர் எவர் தருவாரே: the plea rests on there being no other giver. The circling of the earth recalls the contest for the fruit.

links.note: The song rests its plea on there being no other giver: if Murugan does not grant the boon, who else will (வரம் தராவிடில் பிறர் எவர் தருவாரே). Kural 7 says the mind's anxiety is hard to remove except for those who reach the feet of the incomparable one (தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான்). The hymn's plea is the Kural's claim spoken by one in need of it.
